description: Routing and default inspection rules for the 36 defensive SAST categories.

checks.name: DB Credentials
checks.description: Database connection strings or credential-shaped values may be embedded in source.

default_rule.remediation: Move database credentials to a managed secret store, rotate exposed values, and use least-privilege accounts.

checks.name: .env Files
checks.description: Environment files can contain deployable secrets and should not be committed.

default_rule.remediation: Remove secret-bearing environment files from source control, add safe templates, and rotate any exposed values.

checks.name: Hardcoded Secrets
checks.description: Credential and API-token patterns should not be hardcoded.

default_rule.remediation: Use runtime-injected secrets, redact them from history, and rotate the affected credential.

checks.name: Weak Auth
checks.description: Authentication code may accept weak or bypassable credentials.

default_rule.remediation: Use a vetted identity provider or strong password hashing with MFA and explicit failure handling.

checks.name: Missing Authz
checks.description: Sensitive route handlers may lack an authorization guard.

default_rule.remediation: Enforce server-side authorization for every sensitive operation and verify the resource owner.

checks.name: Cross-User Access
checks.description: Object access may be performed without binding the record to the authenticated user.

default_rule.remediation: Constrain every object lookup by the authenticated principal or an explicit policy decision.

checks.name: Open DB Permissions
checks.description: Database access configuration may grant broad or anonymous permissions.

default_rule.remediation: Apply least privilege, separate read/write roles, and deny anonymous database access by default.

checks.name: Cloud Misconfiguration
checks.description: Cloud resources may be configured for public or overly broad access.

default_rule.remediation: Restrict network and storage policies to required principals and private endpoints.

checks.name: Admin Routes
checks.description: Administrative endpoints require strong authentication and authorization.

default_rule.remediation: Protect admin routes with centralized authorization, network controls, MFA, and audit logging.

checks.name: Debug Tools
checks.description: Debug consoles and development switches should not be exposed in production.

default_rule.remediation: Disable debug tooling in production and gate diagnostics behind authenticated, private controls.

checks.name: Log Leaks
checks.description: Logs may include passwords, tokens, authorization headers, or personal data.

default_rule.remediation: Log structured event metadata only, redact sensitive fields, and apply retention and access controls.

checks.name: Verbose Errors
checks.description: Error responses may expose stack traces or internal implementation details.

default_rule.remediation: Return stable public error codes and keep traces in protected server logs.

checks.name: Git Secrets
checks.description: Git metadata or credential artifacts should not be shipped or committed.

default_rule.remediation: Remove credential artifacts from commits, rotate exposed values, and enforce secret scanning in CI.

checks.name: JavaScript Secrets
checks.description: Browser-bundled JavaScript must not contain privileged secrets.

default_rule.remediation: Keep privileged secrets on the server and expose only narrowly scoped public configuration.

checks.name: Client-only Security
checks.description: Security decisions implemented only in client code can be bypassed.

default_rule.remediation: Repeat all authorization decisions on the server; treat client state as untrusted presentation state.

checks.name: Input Validation
checks.description: Untrusted request data may reach application logic without schema validation.

default_rule.remediation: Validate type, length, format, and allowed values at the trust boundary using a strict schema.

checks.name: SQL Injection
checks.description: SQL statements may be assembled from untrusted input.

default_rule.remediation: Use parameterized queries or a safe query builder and validate identifiers separately.

checks.name: NoSQL Injection
checks.description: User-controlled objects may be passed directly into NoSQL selectors.

default_rule.remediation: Allowlist selector fields and operators, reject object-shaped user input where scalar input is expected.

checks.name: Cross-Site Scripting
checks.description: Untrusted content may be inserted into an HTML or script context.

default_rule.remediation: Use contextual output encoding and safe DOM APIs; sanitize only with a maintained allowlist sanitizer.

checks.name: CSRF
checks.description: State-changing browser requests may lack CSRF protection.

default_rule.remediation: Use SameSite cookies plus framework CSRF tokens or a proven same-origin request defense.

checks.name: Insecure Uploads
checks.description: Uploaded content may be stored or served without type, size, and execution controls.

default_rule.remediation: Allowlist content types, enforce size limits, randomize names, store outside executable paths, and scan content.

checks.name: Path Traversal
checks.description: User-controlled paths may escape the intended directory.

default_rule.remediation: Resolve against a fixed root, verify the resulting path remains within it, and reject traversal segments.

checks.name: SSRF
checks.description: Server-side network requests may target attacker-controlled destinations.

default_rule.remediation: Use destination allowlists, block private/link-local ranges after DNS resolution, and restrict redirects.

checks.name: Password Reset
checks.description: Password reset flows may use predictable or reusable tokens.

default_rule.remediation: Use short-lived, single-use, high-entropy reset tokens and avoid account-existence disclosure.

checks.name: Weak Sessions
checks.description: Session cookies or identifiers may lack secure transport and lifecycle settings.

default_rule.remediation: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite flags; rotate sessions after authentication and privilege changes.

checks.name: JWT Secrets
checks.description: JWT signing may use weak, hardcoded, or algorithm-confusable secrets.

default_rule.remediation: Use managed signing keys, an explicit algorithm allowlist, key rotation, and strict issuer/audience validation.

checks.name: CORS
checks.description: Cross-origin policy may allow arbitrary origins with credentials.

default_rule.remediation: Use an explicit origin allowlist and never combine wildcard origins with credentials.

checks.name: Rate Limits
checks.description: Abuse-sensitive endpoints may lack throttling or lockout controls.

default_rule.remediation: Apply per-IP and per-account limits, exponential backoff, and monitoring to abuse-sensitive operations.

checks.name: Exposed Environments
checks.description: Build or runtime environment values may be exposed to untrusted clients.

default_rule.remediation: Expose only intentionally public configuration and keep secret environment variables server-side.

checks.name: Default Credentials
checks.description: Default administrative credentials or example passwords may remain enabled.

default_rule.remediation: Force unique credentials at provisioning and fail closed when defaults are detected.

checks.name: Unsigned Webhooks
checks.description: Webhook receivers may process requests without authenticity verification.

default_rule.remediation: Verify provider signatures over the raw body, enforce replay protection, and reject unsigned requests.

checks.name: Frontend Payment Checks
checks.description: Payment authorization or amount decisions must not be trusted from frontend state.

default_rule.remediation: Calculate prices and authorize payment server-side; keep private payment keys out of browser bundles.

checks.name: IDOR / BOLA
checks.description: API object identifiers may be accepted without ownership or policy checks.

default_rule.remediation: Authorize access to the specific object using the authenticated principal and tenant boundary.

checks.name: APIs + Input
checks.description: Public APIs should validate request shape and reject unexpected fields.

default_rule.remediation: Use allowlisted request schemas, reject unknown properties, and validate content type and size.

checks.name: Exposed Logs
checks.description: Log files, logging endpoints, or log storage may be publicly reachable.

default_rule.remediation: Keep logs in private storage, restrict access, and avoid serving operational files as static assets.

checks.name: Source Maps
checks.description: Production source maps may reveal proprietary or security-sensitive source.

default_rule.remediation: Keep source maps private or upload them only to protected error-monitoring systems.
